_comment: Default 'Value Column (numeric)' per product type for the Charts page.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: G__GWP_A1A3 stores the GWP against each product's own
declared/functional unit, and that unit is NOT consistent across the dataset —
column G__GWP_FU records it per row and takes values m3, m2, ton, kg, m, m2_R1,
unit. Charting G__GWP_A1A3 for a product type whose rows mix ton with m2 puts
incomparable magnitudes on one axis. The normalised columns (_m2, _m3, _m2R1)
are unit-consistent by construction, so they are the safer default wherever the
product type has mixed declared units and adequate coverage.
HOW TO EDIT: each entry under 'by_product_type' is an ORDERED preference list.
The app picks the first column in the list that (a) is offered by the Value
Column selectbox and (b) has at least 'settings.min_coverage' non-null values in
the rows currently in view. If none qualifies it falls back to
'global_default.value_columns', then to the selectbox's first entry. Reorder the
arrays to change a default; add a product type key to cover a new category.
Keys must match D__ProductType_ENG exactly. Column names must match the
parquet's original (uncleaned) names.
'declared_unit' and 'coverage_2026_07' are documentation only — the app ignores
them. Coverage counts are non-null rows as of the 2026-07 dataset (A__Map_yn=Y)
and are recorded to justify each choice; they are not kept in sync automatically.
Set 'settings.enabled' to false to restore the previous behaviour (fixed
selectbox index) without deleting this file.

settings._comment_group_by: Categorical column used both as the Group By default and as the column read to detect which product type is in view.

global_default._comment: Used when the rows in view span several product types (no single dominant type), or when a type has no entry below.

_comment: Restricts which product types may OFFER a value column in the selectbox at all
(not merely which is preselected). Map a column name to the list of
D__ProductType_ENG values allowed to see it; the column is hidden for every
other type, and also hidden when the rows in view span several types (because
a type-specific basis is not meaningful across a mixed view).
Columns not listed here are always offered. Empty the object to lift all
restrictions.
value_column_visibility._comment_m2R1: GWP per m2 at R=1 normalises for thermal resistance, which only has meaning for insulants. It is populated for a few non-insulation rows but is not a valid comparison basis for them, so it is restricted to Insulation.
value_column_visibility._comment_price_per_R: Cost per unit of thermal resistance, and R itself, are insulation measures: both come from the listino thickness and lambda. The plain list price (PR__Price_EUR_m2) is not restricted.

Adhesives.note: Declared unit is consistently kg, so the FU/DU column is directly comparable.

Binder (Cement).note: Mass-based product, consistently declared per ton. No area/volume normalisation exists.

Building boards.note: Boards are specified and installed by area; per-m2 is the like-for-like comparison.

Coatings.note: Mixed kg/ton declaration; per-m2 coverage too thin to default to. Read with care.

Coil.note: Steel coil is a mass commodity.

Finish (Walls).note: Single row — below min_coverage, so this will normally fall through to the global default.

Framing profiles (Cladding/stud frame).note: Linear product declared per metre; no per-m2/m3 normalisation available.

Grouting.note: Very thin coverage; both options below min_coverage.

In situ Concrete.note: Concrete is specified by volume. Both columns agree here (FU is already m3); the explicit _m3 column is preferred so the axis unit is unambiguous.

Insulation.note: IMPORTANT: insulation rows mix m2, m3 and m2_R1 declarations, so G__GWP_A1A3 is not comparable within this type. Per m2 at R=1 normalises for thermal performance and is the functionally correct basis for comparing insulants of different conductivity and thickness.

Levelling compound.note: Mixed kg/ton declaration — magnitudes differ by 1000x between rows. Consider switching to _m3 manually.

Masonry (Block).note: Four different declared units in one type; per-m2 (walling area) is the usual specification basis.

Metal accessories.note: Predominantly kg; a few rows use a pcs/m2 unit.

Paints.note: No GWP data yet — will fall through to the global default.

Raised access floor.note: Area-based; single row so below min_coverage.

Rebar.note: Reinforcement is priced and specified by mass; per-ton is the industry basis even though _m3 is populated.

Screed.note: Sparse and unit-mixed; neither option is clean. _m3 is the more physically meaningful basis if coverage improves.

Structural components.note: Heterogeneous category (beams, columns, precast) with mixed declarations.

Suspended ceiling.note: Ceiling systems are specified by area.

Tiles.note: Rows mix m2 and kg declarations; per-m2 matches how tiles are specified and has full coverage.

Waterproofing materials.note: Declared per kg; per-m2 also populated and arguably more useful for membranes.

Windows & Doors - Whole system.note: Mixes per-m2 and per-window declarations; per-m2 is comparable across sizes.
